A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a defect-based fault simulation strategy for iDDT testing, which is capable of simulating the effect of defects on iDDT test observables, and is scalable to large designs.

we have developed a practical fault simulation method that enables efficient fault simulation of the DUT for resistive bridging defects and resistive opens, using a combination of linear and non-linear models.

the defect based iDDT fault simulation model is capable of detecting resistive bridging, resistive opens, resistive shorts and resistive opens in series, and is applicable to both combinational and sequential circuits.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a defect-based iDDT fault simulation model that is capable of detecting resistive opens, shorts, and resistive opens with a single power supply transient can be realized by combining linear fault modeling with non-linear simulation.

a practical fault simulation approach for iDDT testing can be realized by partitioning the DUT into two parts, namely, linear and non-linear, and by using the linear model to capture the transient behavior of the DUT.
a defect based fault simulation model is a viable approach to address the challenges associated with testing of manufactured IC’s.
